evals.prompt: I'm writing a physiotherapy blog post about ankle sprains. Can you make one interactive isometric illustration of the lateral ankle ligaments as a single HTML file I can just open? White background, pink anatomy-model look, not a diagram. Show how the anterior talofibular ligament tightens as the foot rolls into inversion and plantarflexion.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page built with the kit and kit/tissue.mjs: the distal tibia and fibula, talus, calcaneus and the anterior talofibular, calcaneofibular and posterior talofibular ligaments, drawn as pink anatomical tissue (bone, cartilage, ligament, a faint skin outline) with no machine parts, base plates or instruments. Bones are turned or lofted with kit/lathe.mjs and smooth-shaded with no tone staircase. Ligaments run from their true attachments and never pass through bone. A small model gives ligament strain from the inversion and plantarflexion angles, the ligament tissue colour follows that strain, and a live readout shows the angles and strain with true numbers. The motion is calm and eased, with pointer and keyboard control. `scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both theme pages, and 4x close-ups of each ligament attachment were taken and looked at.

evals.prompt: We need a figure for our sports-science course site explaining the stretch-shortening cycle in the Achilles tendon during running. Build it as a React component (TSX) we can drop into our Next.js app, and also give me a static HTML preview so I can look at it right now. Dark theme. It should look like a crafted anatomical model, not a chart.
evals.expected_output: A React TSX component (plus any geometry and CSS files) and a standalone dark HTML preview, showing the shank, calcaneus, soleus, gastrocnemius and Achilles tendon as pink anatomical tissue with kit/tissue.mjs. A small model gives tendon length, tendon force and the stored and returned elastic energy over one ground contact; muscle colour follows activation through activationAttrs or setActivation, and the readout comes from the model. The tendon inserts on the posterior calcaneus and the muscle bellies sit in true painter's order around the tibia. Curved tissue shows no tone staircase, fibre lines end on outlines, and `scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0`. 4x close-ups of the tendon insertion and musculotendinous junction were taken and read.

evals.prompt: make an isometric svg of a lumbar vertebra and intervertebral disc showing how the nucleus pulposus moves backwards when you bend forward. for a back-pain clinic landing page. dark, premium, lots of small anatomical detail. just give me the svg file, and a png preview if you can
evals.expected_output: A standalone dark SVG file (styles embedded) of two lumbar vertebrae with the disc between, drawn in the pink tissue palette: vertebral bodies, pedicles, laminae, spinous and transverse processes, facet joints with cartilage, the annulus fibrosus with its lamellae and the nucleus pulposus displaced posteriorly in flexion. No floating labels, no machine parts. Curved surfaces are smooth-shaded without a staircase, every lamella or fibre line ends on an edge or fades, and every overlap is in depth order. A PNG preview plus 4x close-ups of the facets and the disc rim were made and looked at.

evals.prompt: For a biomechanics lecture, make an interactive isometric figure of a sprint start from the blocks: the push-off leg with pelvis, femur, tibia and foot, and the major muscles of hip, knee and ankle extension. Show the force on the block and which muscles fire as the athlete drives out. One HTML file I can open, light theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page built with the kit and kit/tissue.mjs: an anatomical lower limb (pelvis, femur, patella, tibia, fibula, foot bones) with gluteus maximus, hamstrings, vasti, rectus femoris, soleus and gastrocnemius on tendons at their real attachments, and a starting block drawn only as the surface the foot pushes on. A small model gives joint angles, block force and a proximal-to-distal muscle activation sequence, and muscle colour follows activation continuously with no instant switch. Joints rotate about their true centres and nothing passes through anything at any frame. The readout comes from the model, with pointer and keyboard control and an idle loop. The figure was checked with drive.mjs contact sheets slowed with ["slow", 0.2] across the whole push, `line ends: 0` in several poses in both themes, and 4x close-ups of the hip, knee and ankle.

evals.prompt: For an article on flat feet, make an interactive isometric figure of the foot's medial longitudinal arch with the windlass mechanism: show the plantar fascia tightening and the arch rising as the big toe extends at push-off. Lots of fine detail, it should hold up when people zoom in. Standalone HTML, light theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page built with the kit and kit/tissue.mjs: the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuneiforms, first metatarsal, sesamoids and hallux phalanges, the plantar fascia from the medial calcaneal tubercle to the proximal phalanges, and tibialis posterior on its tendon, all as pink anatomical tissue with a faint skin outline and no instruments. A small model gives arch height, navicular drop and fascia tension from the first metatarsophalangeal angle, and the readout uses those numbers. The fascia wraps the metatarsal head without passing through bone, bones are smooth-shaded with no staircase, fibre lines end on outlines, and the motion has no pop. `scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` in both themes, and the response shows 4x close-ups of the metatarsal head, sesamoids and fascia origin were taken in both themes and read.
